deities: Replicas of the 12 Jyotirlingas in the cavern beneath the statue

history.dynasty: Modern (21st-century private construction) - built by builder Arun Tiwari (per trawell.in, jabalpur.com, newandolder.com). CONFLICT (verify): one source (seawatersports.com) says funds were donated by local businessman/philanthropist Shri Rakesh Agrawal and the statue was designed by sculptor Shri Nagji Patel, with construction begun in 2003.
history.period: Construction began 2001 (completed 2004); opened to the public on 15 February 2006. CONFLICT (verify): jabalpur.nic.in (official district site) says the statue was built in 2004; seawatersports.com says construction began 2003 and finished 2006.
history.summary: The Kachnar City Shiva Temple is known for its giant 76-foot (23 m) Lord Shiva statue in a meditative pose, built under the open sky on an artificial cavern that holds replicas of the 12 Jyotirlingas collected from Shiva shrines across India. In front of the Shiva statue stands a statue of Nandi; jet water sprays from the dreadlocks of Shiva. The complex also has idols of Ganesha and the Saptarishi, with landscaped gardens around the hill-top site. Regular morning and evening aartis are held here, making it one of Jabalpur's most visited religious sites. Address per local listings: E 19, Kachnar City Road, Kanchan Vihar, Vijay Nagar, Jabalpur - 482002 (verify).

name: Kachnar City Shiva Temple
town_description: Kachnar City is a locality in the Vijay Nagar area on the outskirts of Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, about 8 km from Jabalpur Junction. The Shiva statue stands on a small hill (Kachnar hill) in Karmeta/Vijay Nagar with landscaped surroundings and a small lake nearby (verify).

travel.airport: Nearest airport is Jabalpur (Dumna/Jabalpur Airport), about 20 km from the temple (per jabalpur.nic.in and jabalpur.com).
travel.railway: Nearest railway station is Jabalpur Junction, about 8 km away (per trawell.in and jabalpur.com).
travel.road: Jabalpur is well connected by road; jabalpur.nic.in notes National Highway-7 passes through Jabalpur. The temple is at Kachnar City Road, Vijay Nagar.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for comfortable weather (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning and evening aarti timings reported as 7 AM and 8 PM daily (trawell.in); one listing reports 7 AM and 7 PM daily (in.worldorgs.com) - conflict, verify. Entry free.
